name: Goliath
bio:
Goliath was a giant warrior from Gath in the Philistine army, standing over nine feet tall, clad in heavy bronze armor, helmet, and leg guards, wielding an iron-tipped spear as thick as a weaver's beam, with a shield-bearer going before him (1 Samuel 17:4-7).

As the Philistine and Israelite armies faced off across the Valley of Elah, Goliath came out every morning and evening for forty days, taunting, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man and let us fight each other." Saul and all Israel heard this and were terrified (1 Samuel 17:8-11, 16). David, arriving at the front lines to visit his brothers, heard the challenge and indignantly rebuked Goliath as an "uncircumcised Philistine" defying "the armies of the living God," and volunteered to fight him (1 Samuel 17:23-26, 32-37).

When the two met, Goliath, seeing only a ruddy young man, despised him and cursed him; David declared he came in the name of the LORD Almighty, then slung a stone that struck Goliath in the forehead, felling the giant. David then drew Goliath's own sword and cut off his head (1 Samuel 17:41-51). Seeing their champion dead, the Philistine army fled in panic, and Israel pursued them to a sweeping victory (1 Samuel 17:51-52). Goliath's defeat remains one of Scripture's most famous illustrations of triumphing over overwhelming force through faith rather than might.
